subject.title: fix(agents): drop stale internal orphan prompts

question: Should OpenClaw fix the stale orphaned-user path by dropping selected internal inter-session leaves in this PR, or prefer the broader state-replay repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90759?
rationale: Both PRs target the same session-state failure class but encode different semantics for old inter-session content, and tests alone do not settle the user-visible runtime behavior.

options.title: Require proof, then choose one repair
options.body: Keep this PR open, require redacted embedded-agent runtime proof for the drop and preserve paths, then compare it against the proof-positive broader repair before merge.

options.title: Adopt the broader state-replay PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90759 as the canonical landing path if maintainers prefer preserving old content as context with state replay.

options.title: Accept this focused predicate
options.body: Proceed with this PR only if maintainers are comfortable dropping all six internal source tools and have equivalent private runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then choose one repair
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open, require redacted embedded-agent runtime proof for the drop and preserve paths, then compare it against the proof-positive broader repair before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The active-turn queued-user merge behavior appears to originate from this area of history, making this the best available routing signal for the repair semantics.
